name: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
ecclesialTitle: Memorial of the Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
briefBio: This memorial celebrates Mary's queenship as wholly received from and subordinate to Christ's kingship. It does not narrate a witnessed coronation, describe a physical crown, or grant Mary independent divine power. Pius XII instituted the feast in 1954 for May 31; the reformed calendar placed it on August 22, following the Assumption. Gospel kingship is service, mercy, truth, and self-giving, never domination or national triumph. Marian prayer supports worship of God, justice, responsibility, and appropriate professional help; it does not guarantee outcomes.

sources.title: Ad Caeli Reginam
sources.reuseBasis: Encyclical used for the institution of the universal feast in 1954 on May 31, the title's roots in Mary's motherhood and association with Christ, maternal service and intercession, and dependence on the divine King; dated royal language is not used to endorse political domination

sources.title: General Audience of 22 August 2012
sources.reuseBasis: Papal catechesis used for the 1954 institution, post-conciliar move to August 22 after the Assumption, Mary's queenship derived from Christ, prayer, and practical confidence without independent Marian power

editorial.reviewer: Catholic Daily factual and theological review

whyItMatters: Mary's queenship is meaningful only within Christ's kingship of truth, mercy, and self-giving service. The memorial challenges domination and invites believers to exercise influence by protecting dignity, seeking justice, and pointing beyond themselves to Christ.
oneMinuteSummary: The August 22 memorial celebrates Mary as Queen because of her relationship to Jesus Christ, the divine King, and her sharing by grace in his paschal victory. Her queenship is created, received, maternal, and wholly dependent on him; it is not a second divine sovereignty or independent power. Pius XII instituted the feast in 1954 for May 31. The post-conciliar calendar moved it to August 22, after the Assumption, emphasizing the link between Mary's glorification and her service beside her Son. The title does not record a witnessed heavenly coronation or prove the details of religious art. Read through the Gospel, kingship means love, truth, mercy, and self-giving rather than domination. The memorial cannot justify monarchy, nationalism, Catholic political supremacy, violence, or contempt for Protestants, Muslims, or any neighbor. Prayer for Mary's intercession accompanies worship of God, justice, responsible action, and professional help; it never guarantees favors or replaces them.

sections.heading: What the memorial celebrates
sections.body: Mary is honored as Queen through her relationship to Christ and participation by grace in his victory. Her dignity is received and creaturely, never divine or independent of him.

sections.heading: A modern feast with older roots
sections.body: Pius XII instituted the universal feast in 1954 on May 31. The reformed calendar placed it on August 22 after the Assumption; this history is liturgical development, not a newly discovered biographical event.

sections.heading: Royalty as Gospel service
sections.body: Christ's reign overturns worldly domination. Marian queenship points toward service, mercy, truth, and the dignity God shares with his people, not hierarchy for its own sake.

sections.heading: Prayer without triumphalism
sections.body: Intercession is not magic, guaranteed success, or a political weapon. Marian prayer must remain compatible with justice, peace, medical and psychological care, and respect for every religious community.

life.gospelTheme: Christ reigns by self-giving love; Mary shares his victory as servant and disciple, directing every honor toward him.
life.struggle: Royal imagery can become domination, nationalism, guaranteed intervention, or a simulated heavenly biography derived from art.
life.response: Keep the title subordinate to Christ, receive the feast's documented liturgical history, and translate royal language into humble service, justice, and nonviolent care.

virtues.name: Humble service
virtues.evidence: Theological interpretation contrasts Gospel royalty with domination and sees Mary's service within Christ and the Church.
virtues.imitation: Use one area of influence to protect another person's voice, dignity, or access instead of increasing your status.

virtues.name: Christ-centered prayer
virtues.evidence: Formal teaching makes Mary's dignity dependent on Christ and links the memorial to his saving work.
virtues.imitation: When asking Mary's intercession, name the responsible action you will take in obedience to Christ.

practice.spiritual: Pray Luke 1:46–49 and notice how Mary's praise directs greatness to God rather than to herself.
practice.action: Give up one small privilege today so another person can speak, participate, receive credit, or obtain needed support.

reflectionQuestions: Does my image of Christian authority resemble Christ's service or worldly domination?
Do I use prayer to deepen responsible action, or to seek control and guaranteed outcomes?

scripture.connection: Mary magnifies God, receives what the Mighty One has done, and models the creaturely praise that keeps her queenship dependent on Christ.

prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, true King of mercy and peace, as we honor Mary your Mother as Queen, free us from domination and empty triumph. Through her intercession make our influence humble, our prayer responsible, and our service faithful to you. Amen.
